what_its_for: Patisiran is used to treat a condition called hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis (hATTR amyloidosis) in adults. This is a rare inherited disease where a faulty protein called transthyretin (TTR) builds up in your body, especially in the nerves and heart, causing damage and symptoms like numbness, tingling, weakness, and problems with your heart, stomach, or bladder. Patisiran works by lowering the amount of this harmful protein your body makes.
how_to_take: Patisiran is NOT a pill you take at home. It is given as an intravenous (IV) infusion — meaning it goes directly into your vein through a needle or catheter. A trained healthcare provider will give you this infusion in a clinic or hospital setting. Each infusion takes about 80 minutes. Before every infusion, your healthcare team will give you pre-medications (such as steroids, antihistamines, and fever reducers like acetaminophen) to help prevent infusion-related reactions. It is very important that you receive these pre-medications before every dose. Stay at the clinic for monitoring after your infusion in case of any reactions.
dosing: The usual dose is based on your body weight. Most adults receive 0.3 mg per kilogram (mg/kg) of body weight once every 3 weeks. Your doctor will calculate the exact dose that is right for you. Do not try to change your dose on your own — always follow your doctor's instructions. Infusions are given every 3 weeks on a regular schedule.
missed_dose: Because patisiran is given by a healthcare provider, it is important to keep all your scheduled appointments. If you miss or need to reschedule an infusion, call your doctor or clinic as soon as possible to set up a new appointment. Try not to delay your treatment for too long. Do not try to 'double up' on doses to make up for a missed one.
storage: You do not need to store patisiran at home — your healthcare provider or clinic handles storage. For reference, the medication must be refrigerated between 36°F and 46°F (2°C and 8°C). It should not be frozen. If you are ever given supplies to take home for any reason, ask your pharmacist or nurse for specific storage instructions.
what_to_avoid: Tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL medications, vitamins, and herbal supplements you take before starting patisiran. Avoid skipping your pre-medications before each infusion, as they help prevent serious reactions. Let your care team know right away if you feel unwell during or after your infusion. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery right after your infusion if you feel dizzy or unwell. Do not start any new medications or supplements without first checking with your doctor.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room right away if you experience: flushing (redness or warmth in your face), chills, feeling faint or dizzy, shortness of breath, chest tightness or chest pain, rapid or irregular heartbeat, nausea or vomiting during or after infusion, redness, swelling, or pain at the injection site, signs of infection such as fever, chills, or unusual tiredness, any new or worsening symptoms of your condition such as increased numbness, tingling, weakness, or falls. Always contact your doctor if you have any concerns or questions about your health.
when_it_works: Patisiran begins to lower the levels of the harmful TTR protein in your blood fairly quickly after starting treatment. However, improvements in your nerve and other symptoms may take several months to become noticeable — for some people it can take 9 to 18 months. It is important to keep going to all your scheduled infusions even if you do not feel better right away. This medicine helps slow down or stop the disease from getting worse, so you may not notice a dramatic change but it is still working to protect your nerves and organs.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of patisiran during pregnancy and breastfeeding is not fully known. Your doctor will help you weigh the risks and benefits. Effective contraception is recommended for women who could become pregnant. Older adults: Patisiran can be used in older adults, but your doctor will monitor you closely for any side effects or reactions. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may monitor your kidney and liver function during treatment. Let your doctor know about any history of liver or kidney disease. Children: Patisiran is currently approved for use in adults only and is not approved for children.
